summary: Use a fallback only when a value is NULL.
documentation: COALESCE returns the first non-NULL argument. It is useful for readable reports when optional fields are missing.
inputs: At least two expressions, evaluated in order.
returns: The first non-NULL value, or NULL if all arguments are NULL.
caution: An empty string and zero are values, not NULL, so they do not trigger the fallback.
scenarios: Show a friendly label when a customer name is missing.
Prefer a mobile number, then an office number.
Replace a missing aggregate with a suitable reporting default.
title: Label unnamed customers
problem: Return id and COALESCE(customer, 'Walk-in') AS customer_label from orders, ordered by id. Preserve empty strings.
goal: Use COALESCE() or an equivalent approach that demonstrates the same concept.
hint: Use COALESCE on customer with the fallback "Walk-in".
